guide.summary: Calendly OAuth is self-serve: you register an app in the developer console and get a client ID and secret, and the docs describe no review step. Composio has a managed Calendly app, so a prototype needs no registration. Own-app setup is mainly about scopes, HTTPS redirect, and saving the secret at creation. Whether a production approval or marketplace review exists is not documented.

composio.note: Managed OAuth2 is available. A GitHub issue (ComposioHQ/composio #4392) reports custom auth configs being refused over derived scopes; this is unverified, so check scopes when you create a custom config.

need_own_app.answer: Not for a prototype or internal tool: the Composio managed app works without registering anything. You need your own app for production branding, custom scopes, dedicated quota or faster trigger polling.
reasons: Users see "Composio wants to access your account" on the consent screen with the managed app
Managed app default scopes may not match what you need; Calendly scopes are fixed per app
Managed apps share quota across all Composio users
Managed auth has a 15-minute minimum polling interval for triggers
Enterprise customers requiring your branding end to end

scenarios.label: Prototype on Composio managed app
scenarios.when_this_applies: Internal tool, prototype or development where the Composio consent screen and default scopes are acceptable.

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count, not measured; no provider registration needed (c1)

scenarios.approval: None for Calendly; Composio provides the OAuth app.

scenarios.label: Own Calendly app, sandbox
scenarios.when_this_applies: You want your own client ID/secret for development, using localhost redirects.

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count, not measured; registration is a self-serve form (c5, c6)

waiting.basis: Docs describe no review for registration (see open questions).

scenarios.label: Own Calendly app, production
scenarios.when_this_applies: Customer-facing agent with your own branding, custom scopes or dedicated quota.

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count, not measured: second app, HTTPS redirect, redirect proxy, Composio config (c6, c8, c9)

waiting.basis: No review or timeline found in the docs read.

scenarios.approval: No production review documented; Partner Marketplace listing may have its own review, unverified.

prerequisites.title: Calendly developer account
prerequisites.detail: Sign up with GitHub or Google. It is separate from your Calendly user account.

prerequisites.title: Composio API key and dashboard access
prerequisites.detail: Needed to create the auth config and copy the redirect URI.

prerequisites.title: HTTPS redirect endpoint (production)
prerequisites.detail: Production redirect URIs must be HTTPS. If you proxy the callback, you need a domain you control.

prerequisites.title: Minimum scope list
prerequisites.detail: Newly created apps have no API access until scopes are requested. Pick the smallest set, e.g. scheduled_events:read, plus webhooks:write if you need webhooks.

prerequisites.title: Paid Calendly plan for webhooks
prerequisites.detail: The subscribing Calendly account needs Standard, Teams or Enterprise to create webhooks. The API itself works on Free.

steps.title: Try the Composio managed app
steps.detail: Check the toolkit for composio_managed_auth_schemes containing OAUTH2, then create a session and connect using the managed app.
steps.done_when: A Calendly account is connected and a tool call succeeds.

steps.title: Decide scopes
steps.detail: Map your agent's tools to the Calendly scope catalog and draft the minimum list. Remember write implies read and webhooks need related read scopes.
steps.done_when: A scope list is written down.

steps.title: Create Calendly developer account and OAuth app
steps.detail: Sign up, create a new OAuth app, choose web or native, choose Sandbox or Production, enter the redirect URI and scopes. Create a separate Production app when going live.
steps.done_when: You see the Client ID, Client Secret and webhook signing key.

steps.title: Save the client secret and webhook signing key
steps.detail: They are shown only once, at creation. Store them in a secrets manager.

steps.title: Get the callback URI from Composio
steps.detail: Copy the redirect URI from your Composio dashboard when creating the auth config. Do not hard-code it.
steps.done_when: You have the Composio callback URI.

steps.title: Optional: set up redirect proxy on your domain
steps.detail: If the browser must stay on your domain, write an endpoint that 302-redirects the callback to Composio, and register that URL as the Calendly redirect URI. Calendly docs do not mention domain verification, so this is for branding only.
steps.done_when: The endpoint returns a 302 to Composio with the query string intact.

steps.title: Register redirect URI in Calendly
steps.detail: Edit the app and set the redirect URI (Composio callback or your proxy). Production must be HTTPS; the URI can be edited later.
steps.done_when: The app is saved with the correct redirect URI.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config with your credentials
steps.detail: Create a custom OAUTH2 auth config for the calendly toolkit with your client ID/secret and the scopes chosen. If the connection fails with scope errors, see the GitHub issue lead.
steps.done_when: The auth config exists and a test connection completes.

steps.title: Check for any production review
steps.detail: No review is documented. Before launch, ask Calendly developer support whether production apps or Partner Marketplace listing need approval, and how long it takes.
steps.done_when: You have a written answer from Calendly.

traps.title: Client secret is shown only once
traps.detail: Editing the app later does not reveal the secret or the webhook signing key.

traps.title: Scopes are fixed per app
traps.detail: Users cannot approve individual scopes in the Composio flow. To change permissions, update the scopes in your app/auth config and reconnect the account.

traps.title: Scopes must be requested explicitly
traps.detail: New OAuth apps get no API access until scopes are requested and approved.

traps.title: Webhooks need a paid plan on the user's side
traps.detail: Free-plan users can use the API but cannot create webhook subscriptions.

traps.title: Tokens get revoked on login changes
traps.detail: Changing the account's email, password or login method revokes tokens, so expect to reconnect.

traps.title: Low rate limits on Free plan
traps.detail: Free plan is 50 requests per user per minute, and only 8 OAuth token requests per user per minute are allowed.

traps.title: Sandbox and Production are separate apps
traps.detail: Calendly recommends creating a second application for Production.

blockers.symptom: 403 missing scopes error on a tool call
blockers.what_it_means: The granted scopes don't cover the endpoint, or the user declined some.
blockers.what_to_do: Add the required scopes to the app and auth config, then reauthorize.
blockers.agent_can_help: Look up the required scopes for the failing endpoint and update the scope list.

blockers.symptom: Custom Calendly auth config can't connect; scopes refused
blockers.what_it_means: A reported Composio issue about derived scopes being refused by the bundled app. Unverified.
blockers.what_to_do: Check that the config's scopes exactly match those on your own Calendly app, and review the GitHub issue.
blockers.agent_can_help: Compare scopes between the auth config and the Calendly app.

blockers.what_it_means: Production apps require HTTPS; http://localhost is only allowed in Sandbox.
blockers.what_to_do: Use an HTTPS URI or switch to a Sandbox app for local testing.

blockers.what_it_means: The Calendly account may be on the Free plan, or webhooks:write and related read scopes are missing.
blockers.what_to_do: Use a Standard/Teams/Enterprise account and grant the needed scopes.

open_questions: Is there a test-user, install or user-count cap for unreviewed production apps? Not found; ask Calendly developer support.
Does a production app or Partner Marketplace listing need review, and how long does it take? Not found; check the Partner Marketplace community post and ask support.
Does Calendly verify redirect URI domain ownership? Not found in the docs read; test with your own domain in Sandbox.
Do Calendly org admins have approval or allowlist controls for end-user installs? Not found; check Calendly help center admin docs.
Sandbox limits are not documented; confirm with support.
The refresh-token rotation guide was not read; single-use refresh tokens may matter for custom setups. Read https://developer.calendly.com/docs/authentication/refresh-token-rotation-guide.md.

claims.text: Composio provides managed OAuth for Calendly, so you do not need to register your own OAuth app.
claims.label: composio_docs

claims.text: Managed apps are suitable for prototypes and development where consent-screen branding doesn't matter.
claims.quote: Users will see "Composio wants to access your account" during OAuth.
claims.label: composio_docs
claims.note: The quote shares few words with this claim. Read it before relying on the claim.

claims.text: You can still create a custom auth config for Calendly for branding, scopes, rate limits or polling intervals.
claims.quote: You can still create a custom auth config for branding, scopes, rate limits, polling intervals, or custom instances.
claims.label: composio_docs

claims.text: Composio's callback is routed via backend.composio.dev, and you can proxy the redirect through your own domain.
claims.quote: If you need to hide Composio's domain, you can proxy the redirect through your own domain instead.
claims.label: composio_docs

claims.text: Calendly's Client Secret and Webhook signing key are only shown at creation.
claims.quote: **Be sure to copy these values as you will not be able to access the Client Secret or Webhook signing key again**.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Production redirect URIs must be HTTPS, and Calendly recommends a separate Production app after starting in Sandbox.
claims.quote: For the Production environment, this must be HTTPS
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Sandbox allows HTTP with a localhost redirect.
claims.quote: For the Sandbox environment, we allow HTTP with localhost domain.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: The redirect URI of an existing OAuth app can be edited.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: The Composio redirect proxy must return a 302 redirect and not follow the redirect server-side.
claims.quote: Your endpoint must return a **302 redirect**.
claims.label: composio_docs

claims.text: No Calendly production review, approval timeline or marketplace review was found in the docs read.
claims.label: unknown

claims.text: Newly created OAuth apps get no API access until scopes are explicitly requested and approved.
claims.quote: For newly created OAuth apps and new Personal Access Tokens, no API access is granted until scopes are explicitly requested and approved.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Webhook payloads require the related read scopes to be granted.
claims.quote: Your app must be granted the related read scopes to receive webhook event payloads.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Creating a webhook subscription requires the Calendly account to be on a paid Standard, Teams or Enterprise plan.
claims.quote: the Calendly user account for which the **webhook subscription** is being made will need a **paid** subscription on the **Standard, Teams**, or **Enterprise** plan.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: In Composio, Calendly scopes are those configured on the OAuth app; users can't approve them individually, and changing them needs a reconnect.
claims.quote: To change Calendly permissions, update the scopes in your OAuth app/auth config and reconnect the account so a new token is issued with the updated scopes.
claims.label: composio_docs

claims.text: A GitHub issue reports Calendly auth configs being unconnectable because derived scopes are refused by the bundled Calendly OAuth app.
claims.label: reported

claims.text: Calendly access tokens are revoked if the account's login email is changed.
claims.quote: The account's login email is changed.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Calendly's Free plan rate limit is 50 requests per user per minute.
claims.quote: | Free Plan    | 50 requests per user per minute  |
claims.label: provider_docs
